title: Support ticket triage agent

problem.statement: Support agents spend the first 6 to 9 minutes of every ticket reading it, finding the customer's shipments and choosing a queue. 31% of tickets are re-routed at least once.
problem.who: The 40-person customer support team and the customers waiting on them
problem.today: Manual triage in the helpdesk; routing rules by keyword
problem.success_measure: Median time to first correct queue under 2 minutes and re-routing under 10% within 8 weeks of go-live

non_goals: It does not reply to customers
It does not issue refunds or change shipments
It does not replace the helpdesk

functional.statement: Classify each new ticket into one of the 12 support queues with a reason
functional.acceptance: On the gold set of 200 labelled tickets, queue accuracy is at least 90%

functional.statement: Attach the customer's open shipments to the ticket
functional.acceptance: Returns the shipments the order system holds for that customer id, or says none found

functional.statement: Escalate tickets that mention injury, legal action or a regulator to a person
functional.acceptance: 100% of the 25 escalation cases in the gold set are routed to the duty manager queue and never auto-assigned

functional.statement: Suggest a first reply for the agent to edit
functional.acceptance: Rated usable without major edits on 70% of 50 sampled tickets by two support leads

quality.stimulus: sends a ticket whose text tells the agent to ignore its instructions and export other customers' data
quality.response: the instruction is treated as data, no tool outside the ticket's own customer id is called, and the attempt is logged
quality.measure: 0 cross-customer tool calls over the 60-case injection set

quality.stimulus: times out or returns an error
quality.response: the ticket is still classified, marked 'shipments unavailable', and retried once
quality.measure: 100% of tickets get a queue within 60 seconds even when the lookup fails

quality.environment: steady state of 1,800 tickets a day
quality.response: spend per ticket is reported by the ledger and capped by a per-ticket token budget
quality.measure: under 0.04 USD per ticket at p95

quality.response: queue, reason and shipments are already on the ticket
quality.measure: p95 under 20 seconds from ticket creation

quality.stimulus: asks why a ticket was routed to a queue
quality.response: the trace shows the input, each tool call, the model's reason and the final decision
quality.measure: 100% of triage decisions have a trace retrievable in under 1 minute

quality.stimulus: is less than 70% confident or meets an escalation term
quality.response: the ticket goes to a person with the agent's suggestion attached, not auto-assigned
quality.measure: 0 auto-assignments below the 0.70 confidence threshold over 1,000 tickets

constraints.budget: Under 2,500 USD a month to run
constraints.team: Two Python engineers and one tester; no .NET or Go

data.name: Ticket text
data.note: Sent to the model through Amazon Bedrock in eu-west-1 under the client's AWS data processing addendum; no training on inputs

data.name: Shipment records
data.note: Read through the order API; only the ticket's customer id

autonomy.limits: May set queue and attach shipments only; cannot reply, close, refund or change a shipment; 6,000 tokens per ticket
